approachQuestion.prompt:
Find labels present in every report

Input: an array reports of R integer arrays. Return all distinct labels that occur in every report, each once, in any order. Repetition inside a report gives no extra credit. There is at least one report; an empty report makes the result empty.

Example 1: reports = [[3,3,7],[7,3,8],[3,7,7]]. Output: [3,7] in any order. Example 2: reports = [[4,4],[4],[]]. Output: []. Example 3: reports = [[2,2,9]]. Output: [2,9] in any order. 1 ≤ R ≤ 200,000; the total number N of label entries is at most 200,000.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Scan reports in order. For each label keep a count of reports credited and the last credited report index; increment only when the current report differs from that saved index. Return keys credited R times.
options.feedback: Occurrences from one report are processed contiguously, so a last-report marker suppresses its duplicates while allowing each later report exactly one contribution.

options.text: Build a distinct-label set for each report in turn and increment a global per-label report count for each set entry. Return keys with count R.
options.feedback: A per-report set also deduplicates contributions. It has the same total expected running-time and auxiliary-space growth as last-report markers.

options.text: Increment one global count for every label occurrence and return labels with count at least R.
options.feedback: For reports [[4,4],[9]], label 4 has two occurrences but is absent from the second report.

options.text: Start with all labels in the first report and remove a candidate whenever one scanned later label differs from it.
options.feedback: reports [[3],[9,3]] must retain 3. Encountering an unrelated value does not prove that a candidate is absent from that report.

feedback.reason: Count contributing containers rather than raw occurrences by recording the last container credited for a key.
details: Maintain a map from label to (creditedReportCount,lastCreditedReport). Process each report in order, crediting a label only on its first occurrence within that report. After all reports, scan map entries and return those with creditedReportCount equal to R. Do not stop early for empty reports.
A label repeated within one report gets only one credit from that report. Compare the last credited report before incrementing; an empty report prevents every label from reaching the required total.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Find labels present in every report — analyzed method”, N is the total number of labels across all R reports and u is their number of distinct values. Output appends have amortized constant cost. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: Visit report headers and entries, then inspect distinct-label aggregates.
details: Count contributing containers rather than raw occurrences by recording the last container credited for a key.
The outer loop visits R reports; inner loops process N entries. The final map scan costs O(u), where u≤N, giving expected O(N+R+1).
O(u+1) for one count/last-report record per distinct label, with output excluded.
“Expected O(N + R + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(N + 1) time independent of R; O(u + 1) space.”: The analyzed method visits each report header even when its array is empty; R need not be bounded by N.
“Expected O(NR + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: It scans each report once, not all reports separately for every candidate.
“Expected O(N + R + 1) time; O(1) space.”: The map may retain u labels and their markers.
